title: Iterator vs ListIterator — forward-only vs bidirectional, add/set during iteration
shortTitle: Iterator vs ListIterator — forward-only vs bidirectional, add/set during iteration

s1_definition.profdef: `Iterator` works on ANY Collection — forward-only (`hasNext()`/`next()`), can only `remove()`. `ListIterator` works ONLY on `List` — bidirectional (`hasNext()`/`next()` + `hasPrevious()`/`previous()`), exposes position (`nextIndex()`/`previousIndex()`), and can `add()` and `set()` during iteration. ListIterator is the ONLY way to safely add/modify elements during iteration without CME. Can start from any index: `list.listIterator(5)` starts at position 5.
s1_definition.oneliner: Iterator = forward-only, remove-only, any Collection. ListIterator = bidirectional, add/set/remove, List only, start at any index.
s1_definition.raw:
**Professional definition:** `Iterator` works on ANY Collection — forward-only (`hasNext()`/`next()`), can only `remove()`. `ListIterator` works ONLY on `List` — bidirectional (`hasNext()`/`next()` + `hasPrevious()`/`previous()`), exposes position (`nextIndex()`/`previousIndex()`), and can `add()` and `set()` during iteration. ListIterator is the ONLY way to safely add/modify elements during iteration without CME. Can start from any index: `list.listIterator(5)` starts at position 5.

**One line to remember:** Iterator = forward-only, remove-only, any Collection. ListIterator = bidirectional, add/set/remove, List only, start at any index.

sections.s3_banking:
At the National Bank of India, the engineering team hit a real problem that maps directly onto Iterator versus ListIterator. Rajesh (account SAV2001, a software engineer with a savings balance of 1,000,000 rupees) and Priya (account CUR3001, a property owner with a current balance of 250,000 rupees) both run operations that stress the system's collection handling, and the wrong data-structure choice here caused slow lookups, lost entries, or incorrect ordering in production reports.

The mini-project below reproduces that banking scenario and shows exactly how Iterator versus ListIterator solves it correctly, using BigDecimal for every money value and the same Account model with debit and credit behaviour.
sections.s5_journey:
The input is a list of transactions traversed first with an Iterator and then with a ListIterator.

**Step 1.** A plain `Iterator` moves forward only with `next()`, reading Rajesh's transactions one by one and allowing deletion via `remove()`.

**Step 2.** A `ListIterator` adds `hasPrevious()` and `previous()`, so it can walk backward as well and revisit Priya's earlier entries.

**Step 3.** During the ListIterator pass, `set()` updates the current element and `add()` inserts a new one in place, giving full bidirectional edit control that the basic Iterator lacks.
sections.s5b_flow:
```text
  Input: Rajesh SAV2001 (Rs.1,000,000), Priya CUR3001 (Rs.250,000)
    │
    ▼
  Service layer (applies Iterator versus ListIterator)
    │  loads accounts into the collection
    │  performs the operation (add / lookup / order / dedup)
    ▼
  Collection state changes
    │  SAV2001 and CUR3001 processed with BigDecimal amounts
    ▼
  Output: correct result returned to the caller
```
sections.s5c_hld:
```
  LEDGER EDITING SERVICE (bidirectional cursor)
  ┌──────────────┐   ┌───────────────────────────┐
  │ Reconcile    │──▶│ LedgerEditor              │
  │ Job          │   │  ListIterator over entries│
  └──────────────┘   │  forward: next()          │
                     │  back:    previous()       │
                     │  fix:     set() / add()    │
                     └────────────┬───────────────┘
                                  ▼
                     ┌───────────────────────────┐
                     │ LinkedList<LedgerEntry>   │ O(1) at cursor
                     └───────────────────────────┘
  Only ListIterator can mutate during iteration (no CME)
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
Iterator is the basic forward-only cursor for any Collection — `hasNext()/next()/remove()`. ListIterator extends Iterator for Lists only — adds backward traversal (`hasPrevious()/previous()`), insertion (`add()`), replacement (`set()`), and position tracking (`nextIndex()/previousIndex()`). ListIterator is the ONLY way to add/modify elements during iteration without CME. LinkedList benefits most from ListIterator — O(1) add/remove at current position.
